newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police use explosive to seize Corsica suspects.
newsitem.headline: French police use explosive to seize Corsica suspects.

text.p: A special French police unit used explosives to burst into a house in southern Corsica and detain three brothers suspected of machinegunning a police station last month, gendarmerie police said on Saturday.

Officers of the paramilitary gendarmerie police, including members of the RAID rapid intervention unit, seized the three on Friday at their home in the village of Urbalacone south of the island capital Ajaccio.
The officers had used explosives to blow open the front door and found two rifles and ammunition.
The brothers are suspected of taking part in the attack on the Sainte Marie Sicche gendarmerie barracks on December 27. A gendarme had returned fire but apparently without hitting the attackers' car.
Investigators said the suspects were not believed to be linked to separatists who have recently stepped up their 20-year-campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.

Corsica has been trying to shake off a reputation for lawlessness -- murder rates are far higher than on the mainland. In 1996, there were 22 killings on the island of 250,000 people, down from 40 in 1995.
